Commentary.Commentary: We are back for the chase! The players are already in the middle now. Hayley Matthews and Qiana Joseph are the two openers for West Indies Women. Lauren Bell to start proceedings with the ball. Here we go...
... THE RUN CHASE ...

Right then, England Women have got runs on the board in this crucial game and it is always a good thing. This is the last game of the group stage and it is a shootout between these two sides because after all the calculations, it is confirmed that South Africa Women have qualified for the semi-final from this group and only one spot remains now. The Windies will have to give their all here while England Women have enough quality to stop them. A huge run chase is coming up shortly. Whose side are you on?

Afy Fletcher is up for a chat. She says that she was trying to keep it simple and kept her lengths tight. She continues that her team needs to keep it simple while batting as well. Ends up saying they need to be calm and composed to chase the score down.

West Indies Women, on the other hand, will be a bit disappointed because they were excellent in the Powerplay but allowed England Women to take control of the game. Hayley Matthews also missed a trick as she introduced her strike bowler, Karishma Ramharack in the 14th over but in reality, she should have come much earlier. Deandra Dottin was fantastic in the field taking a couple of good catches and forcing a fine run out as well, but they did miss quite a few chances as well. Afy Fletcher was the pick of the bowlers picking up 3 wickets and giving away just 21 runs. Dottin and Matthews chipped in with one each.

England Women took their time to adjust to the conditions of Dubai as this was their first game of the tournament in this stadium. It wasn't a great Powerplay and they lost more than one wicket in that phase for the first time in this World Cup. Both the openers got starts but failed to convert it as they found themselves in a difficult situation. The rescue act began with Nat Sciver-Brunt and skipper Heather Knight joining hands at the crease. They decided to keep rotating the strike and not play too many dot balls. However, just when things were looking good, Knight had to leave the field due to an injury after scoring 21 off just 13 balls and adding 46 runs along with her partner. The pressure then came on Nat Sciver-Brunt who flourished with a brilliant half-century taking them over the 140-run mark.

A finish with a flurry for England Women! Nat Sciver-Brunt has once again produced an amazing knock when her team needed it the most. She remained unbeaten on 57 off 50 which could prove to be the difference in this game. Windies have a tough job on their hands, but if they want to continue their journey, they have to chase down this total.

Oh dear, that was a teasing delivery, slowed up, on middle and leg, Nat Sciver-Brunt looks for the reverse scoop but is totally undone by the lack of pace on it. The ball deflects off her waist and goes behind the keeper to her right for a leg bye. England Women end at 141/7!

Commentary.Commentary: Right then, with all the pre-match formalities wrapped up, it’s time for the action to begin! The two umpires stride to the middle as West Indies gather for one final huddle, with Hayley Matthews delivering a last burst of motivation. Fired up and ready, they take their positions on the field.  Out come England’s openers, Danni Wyatt-Hodge and Maia Bouchier, determined to set the tone yet again for England Women! West Indies Women have decided to start with pace straight up and it will be Chinelle Henry to start for them with the new ball in hand! Away we go!

With the final group stage showdown just moments away, Heather Knight and Hayley Matthews lead their teams onto the field, hearts pounding and spirits high, for the national anthems. The West Indies’ anthem will thunder through the stadium first, followed by England’s!

PITCH REPORT - Anjum Chopra is joined by Lisa Sthalekar at the middle for the pitch analysis. Anjum starts by saying that the temperature is in the mid-30s while the breeze flowing across will assist the pacers a bit. Adds that the square boundaries are 53 meters and 63 meters while the straight one is 73 meters which will need great timing to be cleared. Lisa joins in and says England will have to adapt to this venue where they haven't played yet and pace has troubled them in the past. Mentions Chinelle Henry could trouble their batters with that tight line and upset England who might want to post somewhere around that 140-run mark.

Heather Knight, the captain of England Women, says that she would like to bowl first but they won't mind batting first as the pitch is a bit dry. She continues that they have a good momentum from the past couple of games and they would bring their best cricket to achieve the results. Ends up saying that Alice Capsey comes back into the playing XI.

Hayley Matthews, the skipper of West Indies Women says that they have been quite successful chasing and want to stick to that strength. Adds that they just want to go out and play the best brand of cricket and look to win. Mentions that there are two changes on the side with Chedean Nation coming in and with Stafanie Taylor missing out they have added more depth to their batting with the other change.

England Women (Playing XI) - Danni Wyatt-Hodge, Maia Bouchier, Alice Capsey (In place of Sophia Dunkley), Nat Sciver-Brunt, Heather Knight (C), Amy Jones (WK), Dani Gibson, Sophie Ecclestone, Charlie Dean, Sarah Glenn, Lauren Bell.

West Indies Women (Playing XI) - Hayley Matthews (C), Qiana Joseph, Shemaine Campbelle (WK), Deandra Dottin, Chinelle Henry, Aaliyah Alleyne, Chedean Nation (In place of Stafanie Taylor), Zaida James (In place of Mandy Mangru), Afy Fletcher, Ashmini Munisar, Karishma Ramharack.
TOSS - West Indies Women have won the toss and elected to BOWL first.

For West Indies Women, this is a must-win game if they are to advance. With a superior net run rate compared to South Africa, a victory here would guarantee them a place in the knockout stages. While Hayley Matthews and Stafanie Taylor have stepped up in crucial moments, especially in their win over Bangladesh, the rest of the batting order needs to deliver when it matters most. Their bowling, led by Matthews, Karishma Ramharack, and Afy Fletcher, has been consistent in picking up wickets, but they face a tough task in containing England's in-form lineup. Will England complete the group stages with an unbeaten record, or will the Windies rise to the occasion and spoil the party? Stay tuned for toss updates and the exciting action to follow!

England Women have been in tremendous form, sitting comfortably at the top of Group B with three wins from three games. Their batting has been led by the brilliant Danni Wyatt-Hodge, who has already amassed over 130 runs in the tournament. Nat Sciver-Brunt has shown her class too, rescuing the team from tricky situations, as seen in their last match against South Africa. Their bowling unit, with the likes of Sophie Ecclestone and Sarah Glenn, has been relentless in restricting opposition batters. Skipper Heather Knight has done an outstanding job in keeping the team well-balanced and focused on their ultimate goal of securing a spot in the semi-finals.

The ICC Women's T20 World Cup is heating up as we approach the semi-finals, and Group B has everything to play for. England Women, unbeaten and top of the table, are up against West Indies Women in a high-stakes clash. A win for the English secures their semi-final spot, but if they slip and lose big, not only could West Indies sneak through, but England might also face a shock exit if their NRR takes a hit. England Women are one of the most in-form teams in the tournament, and their batting has been explosive. Their last match saw openers Danni Wyatt-Hodge and Maia Bouchier chase down 110 with ease, both scoring unbeaten fifties. Skipper Heather Knight and Amy Jones add further steel to the middle order, while Nat Sciver-Brunt’s all-around brilliance makes her a game-winner in both departments. With a spin-heavy attack, Sophie Ecclestone has been superb, supported by Sarah Glenn and Charlie Dean, making England a formidable force. West Indies Women, meanwhile, are in a do-or-die situation. Despite pressure, their squad has shown fight. Karishma Ramharack stole the show in their last game with a four-fer, while Chinelle Henry delivered a match-winning all-round performance against Scotland Women. Captain Hayley Matthews, a threat with both bat and ball, will be hoping to inspire her side, and the return of Deandra Dottin has given the team a massive boost. Veterans like Shemaine Campbelle and Stafanie Taylor, part of the 2016 World Cup-winning squad, know what it takes to win big games, but they'll need the likes of Qiana Joseph, Aaliyah Alleyne, and Afy Fletcher to step up when it matters most. Will the Windies pull off a stunning performance to keep their campaign alive? Or will England’s unbeaten run carry them through to the semis? A thrilling contest awaits with everything on the line!
